APT-ENG-0051: The error lies in segment (B) 'taken back by'. The correct idiom meaning shocked or surprised is 'taken aback', not 'taken back'. APT-ENG-0052: The error lies in segment (D) 'obliged of my friend'. The adjective 'obliged' takes the preposition 'to' when referring to a person, not 'of'. Correct sentence: 'I am very much obliged to my friend for the help he rendered to me.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0053: The error lies in segment (C) 'I used to eat into'. The phrasal verb 'eat into' means to consume resources or savings. APT-ENG-0054: The error lies in segment (A) 'Mathematics help'. Correct sentence: 'Mathematics helps in developing the logical mindset of students.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0055: The error lies in segment (A) 'very sweet'. The verb 'sings' must be modified by an adverb of manner ('sweetly'), not an adjective ('sweet'). Correct sentence: 'Rahul sings very sweetly when he is in a good mood.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0056: The error lies in segment (D) 'write her'. In the future continuous tense ('will be + V-ing'), the main verb must take the present participle form ('writing'). Correct sentence: 'She will be writing her examination by this time tomorrow.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0057: The error lies in segment (D) 'until the last house'. 'Until' is a preposition of time. Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0058: The error lies in segment (C) 'The workers called out'. The correct phrasal verb meaning to cancel or withdraw an ongoing action or strike is 'call off', not 'call out'. Correct sentence: 'The workers called off the strike because the management acceded to all their demands.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0059: The error lies in segment (B) 'and cannot be put on'. The phrasal verb meaning to postpone or defer is 'put off', whereas 'put on' means to wear or produce. Correct sentence: '...as they require quick action and cannot be put off.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0060: The error lies in segment (D) 'I had seen'. When a specific past time marker is given ('yesterday'), the simple past tense ('saw') must be used rather than the past perfect tense ('had seen'). Correct sentence: 'I saw her with her mother in the cinema hall yesterday.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0061: The error lies in segment (A) 'she would'. This sentence follows the first conditional structure (real present/future condition): 'If + simple present (exercises), ... will + V1 (will remain)'. The modal 'would' is used for hypothetical conditionals (type 2). Correct sentence: 'If she exercises daily, she will remain energetic and fit forever.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0062: The error lies in segment (C) 'like good'. The singular countable noun 'cup' requires an indefinite article 'a'. The correct phrase is 'like a good cup of coffee'. Correct sentence: 'In this cold weather, there’s nothing like a good cup of coffee.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0063: The error lies in segment (B) 'she look up'. The sentence describes events in the past ('saw', 'it was getting dark'). APT-ENG-0064: The error lies in segment (A) 'ate his food'. The time phrase 'Since childhood' paired with the present/future consequence 'and he will not change' indicates a habitual action continuing up to the present, requiring present tense ('eats') or present perfect ('has eaten'). Correct sentence: 'Since childhood, Monty has eaten his food fast and he will not change.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0065: The error lies in segment (D) 'Until I was'. The sentence expresses contrast or concession: walking home despite weakness. The subordinating conjunction 'Until' indicates a time limit. APT-ENG-0066: The error lies in segment (C) 'of association on Saturday'. The noun 'association' is a specific countable entity here and requires the definite article 'the' ('of the association'). APT-ENG-0067: The error lies in segment (B) 'come to football,'. APT-ENG-0068: The error lies in segment (C) 'He do not'. The third-person singular pronoun 'He' agrees with the singular auxiliary verb 'does not', not 'do not'. Correct sentence: 'He does not fear the repercussions of this decision.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0069: The error lies in segment (C) 'Jerry driving'. APT-ENG-0070: The error lies in segment (B) 'and his friends comes'. The subject 'his friends' is plural and takes the plural verb 'come', not the singular form 'comes'. Correct sentence: 'He organises a children’s fair every year and his friends come to attend it.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0071: There is no grammatical error in the sentence. 'The meeting was called off' correctly uses the phrasal verb meaning cancelled, and the prepositional phrase 'due to a medical emergency of the manager' is syntactically sound. Hence, option D ('No error') is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0072: The error lies in segment (B) 'accused in'. The verb 'accuse' takes the preposition 'of', not 'in'. The correct collocation is 'accused of doing/not doing something'. APT-ENG-0074: The error lies in segment (A) 'cover above a table'. For safety during an earthquake, one takes shelter beneath furniture. The preposition 'above' should be 'under'. APT-ENG-0075: The error lies in segment (C) 'a public sector bank is high than that at'. APT-ENG-0076: The error lies in segment (D) 'hardly picture in Rome I was unable'. APT-ENG-0077: The error lies in segment (C) 'looked decently'. APT-ENG-0078: The error lies in segment (A) 'watch an movie'. The noun 'movie' begins with a consonant sound (/m/), requiring the indefinite article 'a' rather than 'an'. Correct sentence: 'Would you like to watch a movie tonight at eight?' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0079: The error lies in segment (B) 'that angry'. The correlative construction expressing cause and effect is 'so + adjective + that + clause', not 'that + adjective + that'. APT-ENG-0080: The error lies in segment (A) 'his father beat him'. The verb phrase 'can't stand' is followed by a gerund structure (noun/pronoun + '-ing'). Therefore, 'beat' should be 'beating'. APT-ENG-0081: The error lies in segment (D) 'careful while executed the'. APT-ENG-0089: The error lies in segment (B) 'shall been holding a meeting'. APT-ENG-0091: The error lies in segment (A) 'a oasis is an area'. The noun 'oasis' begins with a vowel sound (/oʊ/), requiring the indefinite article 'an' rather than 'a'. APT-ENG-0092: The error lies in segment (B) 'a American'. The word 'American' begins with a vowel sound (/ə/), which requires the indefinite article 'an', not 'a'. Correct sentence: 'Emily is an American living in Paris for her work.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0093: The error lies in segment (A) 'gave out prizes'. The conventional phrasal verb for distributing honors or awards at an official ceremony is 'give away' (past tense 'gave away').
